title: B2+ · L42 — Politics vocabulary
description: Vocabulario politico: legislation, coalition, bipartisan, filibuster, y estructuras democraticas.

questions.prompt: Un comentarista politico distingue entre discurso y ley.
questions.question: 'Legislation' means:
options: A political speech in parliament.
Laws made by a legislative body (parliament, congress).
The process of a national election.
A general political debate.
questions.explanation: Legislation = leyes creadas por un cuerpo legislativo (parliament, congress). Central en political discourse. Registro: politico-formal, ubicuo. Colocaciones clave: 'piece of legislation' (una ley concreta), 'pass legislation' (aprobar), 'draft legislation' (redactar), 'sweeping legislation' (amplia, transformadora), 'landmark legislation' (historica). Distinguirlo de 'bill' (proyecto de ley, todavia no aprobado) y 'law' (ya aprobada y en vigor). Error hispano: pronunciar como 'legis-la-cion' — es /ˌledʒɪsˈleɪʃən/ con acento en 'LEI'. Familia: 'legislator', 'legislature', 'legislative'.
examples: Congress passed sweeping healthcare legislation after months of negotiation. → dato de news
The bill became legislation after the Senate vote and the president's signature. → proceso completo

questions.prompt: En una votacion senatorial se destaca lo inusual.
questions.question: 'Bipartisan' describes:
options: Support from a single party only.
Support from both major political parties.
An alliance of two different countries.
A vote held in two separate elections.
questions.explanation: Bipartisan = con apoyo de ambos partidos principales (US: Democrats + Republicans; UK: Labour + Conservative). Termino de aprobacion moderada en un contexto politico polarizado. Registro: politico-analitico. Familia: 'partisan' (opuesto — de un solo partido, conflictivo), 'nonpartisan' (neutro, sin filiacion). CRECIENTEMENTE RARO en US post-2010, lo cual hace el termino cargado de nostalgia. 'Bipartisan compromise' se cita como valor democratico perdido. Error hispano: escribir 'bipartizan' o 'bi-partisan' (con guion) — la forma standard es 'bipartisan' junto.
examples: The infrastructure bill passed with rare bipartisan support — 20 Republicans crossed the aisle. → dato politico
Bipartisan cooperation is harder to find than at any point in recent memory. → analisis contemporaneo

questions.statement: A 'coalition' government is formed when multiple parties join together to hold power.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Coalition = alianza multi-partido para formar gobierno cuando ningun partido tiene mayoria absoluta. Comun en sistemas parlamentarios con representacion proporcional (Germany, Netherlands, Israel, Sweden, Ireland). Menos comun en two-party first-past-the-post system como US o UK (aunque UK tuvo coalition 2010-2015 Conservative-Lib Dem). Registro: politico-institucional. Familia: 'minority government' (gobierna sin mayoria, negocia caso por caso), 'grand coalition' (los dos partidos grandes juntos — comun en Germany), 'coalition talks' (negociaciones para formar). Error hispano: pronunciar como 'coa-li-cion' — /ˌkoʊəˈlɪʃən/ con acento en 'LI'.
examples: Germany's coalition government includes three parties — traffic-light coalition, they called it. → ejemplo europeo
The coalition collapsed after months of policy disagreement over energy. → dinamica tipica

questions.prompt: Un analista politico americano explica una tactica parlamentaria unica.
questions.question: 'Filibuster' is:
options: The process of voting quickly.
A parliamentary tactic of prolonged speech (or the threat of it) to delay or block a vote.
Political bribery or corruption.
The act of winning an election decisively.
questions.explanation: Filibuster = obstruccion parlamentaria via discurso interminable (o su amenaza). Iconico del US Senate. Regla actual: requiere 60 votos (de 100) para 'invocar cloture' — es decir, cortar el debate y forzar votacion. En la practica: cualquier ley controvertida necesita 60 votos, no 51. Muy controversial: unos ven en el una proteccion de minorias, otros como veto de bloqueo permanente. Registro: politico-institucional US. Filibusters historicos: 24 horas de Strom Thurmond contra el Civil Rights Act (1957). Error hispano: 'filibustero' en espanol tiene otro sentido (pirata) — en anglo politico es solo la tactica parlamentaria.
examples: Senators filibustered for 24 hours to block the civil rights bill in the 1950s. → dato historico
Some argue the filibuster needs reform; others see it as a check on the majority. → debate contemporaneo

questions.text: The proposed legislation would require sixty votes in the Senate to overcome a potential filibuster.
questions.explanation: Frase clasica de political journalism US. 'Proposed legislation', 'sixty votes', 'overcome filibuster' — colocaciones precisas del Senate procedure. Feature de connected speech: 'sixty votes' /ˈsɪksti voʊts/ — la /t/ intermedia se suaviza a flap en americano (/ˈsɪksdi/); 'overcome a' encadena /oʊvərˈkʌmə/ con weak form del articulo. 'Would require' es conditional que expresa procedimiento hipotetico. Registro: political-institutional journalism. Familia: 'cloture vote' (voto para cerrar debate), 'nuclear option' (cambiar reglas por mayoria simple).
examples: Any spending bill needs sixty votes to break a filibuster in the current Senate. → norma procedimental
The bill fell three votes short of overcoming the filibuster — dead for this session. → resultado tipico

questions.prompt: Se analiza como surge un movimiento politico exitoso.
questions.question: 'Grassroots' movement means:
options: Movement led by the government from above.
Movement starting organically from ordinary citizens at the local level.
Movement funded by wealthy elites.
Movement organized by corporate lobbies.
questions.explanation: Grassroots (literal: 'raices del cesped') = movimiento organico desde la base ciudadana, sin direccion top-down. Opuesto a 'top-down' (dirigido desde arriba) y 'astroturf' (movimiento aparentemente grassroots pero orquestado por intereses ocultos — juego de palabras con 'AstroTurf', hierba artificial). Registro: politico-activista. Familia: 'grassroots organizing', 'grassroots campaign', 'grassroots donations' (pequenas donaciones de muchos ciudadanos, no de un donor grande). Error hispano: escribir 'grass roots' (dos palabras) o 'grass-root' (singular) — el standard es 'grassroots' junto, invariable.
examples: The campaign started as a true grassroots movement — coffee shops, church basements, neighborhood chats. → autenticidad
Grassroots organizing beat the well-funded incumbent — a David-and-Goliath story. → caso clasico

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino politico con su equivalente en espanol:
questions.explanation: Vocabulario politico esencial. Precisiones utiles: 'constituency' = area geografica que representa un politico (UK) O los votantes que le apoyan (US, mas amplio); 'incumbent' /ɪnˈkʌmbənt/ = el actual ocupante del cargo, se dice tanto de presidents como de MPs, senators, mayors — tienen ventaja en reelecciones ('incumbency advantage'). 'Referendum' plural: 'referenda' (formal, latin) o 'referendums' (mas comun en periodicos). Registro: politico-institucional. Error hispano: escribir 'referendum' con acento — en anglo va sin acento.
examples: The incumbent has a slight edge in the polls — name recognition matters a lot. → dinamica electoral
The MP visited every corner of the constituency in the run-up to the vote. → practica politica

questions.target: The polarization between the two parties has reached historic highs, making bipartisan legislation increasingly rare.
questions.explanation: Analisis politico maduro tipo Beltway journalism. 'Polarization' (nominalizacion), 'historic highs' (colocacion), 'bipartisan legislation increasingly rare' — sound bite condensado. Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'highs,', enfasis tonico en 'historic' y en 'increasingly'; tono descendente en 'rare'. Contracciones no aplican en registro analitico serio. Registro: political analysis / opinion column. Familia: 'polarized electorate', 'political tribes', 'affective polarization' (la variante donde odias al otro lado emocionalmente, no solo discrepas). Formula transferible: X + causa + consequence.
examples: Partisan gridlock has stalled meaningful reform for the better part of a decade. → diagnostico institucional
Bipartisan compromise is politically toxic in the current climate — voters punish it. → analisis electoral

questions.prompt: Un politologo describe un fenomeno global reciente.
questions.question: 'Populism' refers to:
options: Simple popularity contests.
Political appeal that opposes 'the ordinary people' to a corrupt 'elite'.
Any democratic movement.
The economic doctrine of communism.
questions.explanation: Populismo = estilo politico que construye un antagonismo entre 'el pueblo comun' (virtuoso) y una 'elite corrupta' (culpable). Puede ser IZQUIERDA (Chavez, Podemos, Sanders) o DERECHA (Trump, Le Pen, Meloni, Orban). Analizado extensivamente en political science moderno (Cas Mudde, Jan-Werner Muller). Registro: politico-academico. NO es sinonimo de 'demagogia' ni de 'autoritarismo', aunque puede solaparse. Error hispano: usar 'populist' con carga automaticamente negativa — en analisis anglo puede ser descriptivo neutral. Familia: 'populist rhetoric', 'populist movement', 'anti-establishment'.
examples: Right-wing populism surged in Europe after the 2015 migration crisis. → contexto historico
Populist rhetoric divides society into 'us' and 'them' — that's its defining move. → mecanismo retorico

questions.statement: 'Gerrymandering' is the practice of drawing electoral district boundaries to favor one political party.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Gerrymandering /ˈdʒɛriˌmændərɪŋ/ = manipulacion de mapas electorales para ventaja partidista. Del nombre de Elbridge Gerry, gobernador de Massachusetts en 1812 que aprobo un distrito con forma de salamandra ('Gerry-mander'). Practica antidemocratica extendida en US (donde los legislativos estatales suelen dibujar los mapas de su propio Congreso). Registro: politico-critico. Tecnicas: 'packing' (concentrar votantes del rival en un distrito para desperdiciar votos), 'cracking' (diluir votantes del rival entre varios distritos). En muchas democracias europeas los mapas los hace una comision independiente para evitarlo. Error hispano: pronunciar la 'g' como en 'girar' — es /dʒ/ como en 'juice'.
examples: Gerrymandering can turn a 50-50 state into safe seats for the majority party. → efecto
Courts have struck down some of the most egregiously gerrymandered maps as unconstitutional. → check judicial

questions.prompt: Un presidente actua sin esperar al Congress.
questions.question: 'Executive order' is:
options: An order to place at a restaurant.
A directive from a president or executive with the force of law, issued without needing legislation.
A law passed by the legislative branch.
A ruling issued by the judicial branch.
questions.explanation: Executive order = directive presidencial con fuerza de ley, dentro de los limites de la autoridad ejecutiva. No requiere Congress. Usado extensivamente por US presidents modernos (Obama, Trump, Biden). CRITICA constitucional: puede rozar la separacion de poderes si excede autoridad delegada. LIMITE practico: cada president puede REVERTIR los executive orders del anterior con nuevos executive orders — herramienta reversible. Registro: politico-institucional. Familia: 'presidential proclamation', 'signing statement', 'memorandum'. Error hispano: pronunciar 'executive' como en espanol — es /ɪɡˈzekjətɪv/ con la 'x' como /gz/.
examples: The president signed an executive order on climate emissions his first week in office. → uso simbolico y sustantivo
Executive orders can be reversed by future administrations — they're not laws. → reversibilidad clave

questions.text: The Supreme Court's ruling upheld the law but limited its scope significantly in a five-to-four decision.
questions.explanation: Frase clasica de reporting judicial US. 'Supreme Court', 'ruling', 'upheld the law' (declaro valida la ley), 'limited its scope' (redujo el alcance), 'five-to-four decision' (voto 5-4, cerrado). Feature de connected speech: 'Supreme Court's ruling' /suːˈpriːm kɔːrts ˈruːlɪŋ/ con /s/ del posesivo; 'upheld' /ʌpˈheld/ — la 'h' se aspira suave. 'Five-to-four' con enlazado /faɪvtəˈfɔːr/. Registro: legal-journalistic. Familia: 'strike down' (opuesto — declarar inconstitucional), 'majority opinion', 'dissent', 'concurring opinion', 'precedent'.
examples: The Court struck down the law in a landmark six-to-three ruling. → decision unanime del bloque conservador
The decision narrows but does not fully overturn established precedent. → matiz juridico

questions.prompt: Analista electoral explica donde se concentran las campanas US.
questions.question: 'Swing state' means:
options: A politically stable, predictable state.
A state where the outcome of an election is genuinely uncertain.
Any state at all.
Only a rural state.
questions.explanation: Swing state = estado donde el resultado es incierto y suele decidirse por margenes estrechos. En US: Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin, Arizona, Georgia, Nevada — la lista cambia con el tiempo. Las campanas concentran DINERO y VISITAS ahi porque el Electoral College hace que solo unos pocos estados 'importen' realmente. Contrasta con 'safe state' (previsible: California para Democrats, Texas para Republicans, historicamente). Registro: politico-electoral. Familia: 'battleground state' (sinonimo), 'purple state' (mezcla de rojo republicano y azul democrata), 'toss-up' (empate segun encuestas). Error hispano: traducir literal 'estado columpio' — no se dice.
examples: Pennsylvania is a critical swing state — its 19 electoral votes could decide the presidency. → dato estrategico
Both candidates are pouring money into swing states while ignoring the safe ones. → logica de campana

questions.statement: 'Impeachment' is the same thing as removing a public official from office.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Confusion masiva. Impeachment = ACUSACION formal por parte de la camara baja (House). El removal (destitucion) es proceso SEPARADO en la camara alta (Senate) donde se requiere 2/3 de mayoria. Un official puede ser IMPEACHED (acusado) sin ser CONVICTED (destituido) — de hecho, ningun presidente US ha sido convicted en la historia. Registro: politico-legal US. Error hispano generalizado: usar 'impeachment' como sinonimo de 'destitucion' — no lo es. Andrew Johnson (1868), Bill Clinton (1998), Donald Trump (2019 y 2021) fueron impeached pero absueltos por el Senate. Familia: 'articles of impeachment' (los cargos), 'impeachment trial', 'acquit' (absolver), 'convict' (condenar/destituir).
examples: Impeachment is charging; conviction is removing — they're two separate steps. → distincion precisa
Two US presidents were impeached but not convicted — no president has ever been removed. → dato historico

questions.target: The legislation faces an uphill battle in the Senate, where partisan divisions have hardened over recent years.
questions.explanation: Discurso politico maduro tipo Beltway journalism. 'Uphill battle' (colocacion — camino cuesta arriba, dificil pero no imposible), 'partisan divisions have hardened' (verbo dinamico), 'over recent years' — sintagma temporal profesional. Ritmo natural: pausas breves entre clausulas, enfasis tonico en 'uphill', 'partisan', 'hardened'. Contracciones no aplican en registro analitico. Registro: political analysis / opinion piece. Formula muy comun: el sujeto (bill / candidate / policy) enfrenta un contexto (contexto adverso), con causa historica.
examples: The bill's chances in the House are slim — the Speaker has already signaled resistance. → forecast politico
Passage would require crossing party lines — increasingly rare and increasingly costly for those who try. → analisis dinamico
